title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 383
paragraphs: The following privilege was specially granted to this class, and to no others of the Egyptians except the priests: each man had twelve yokes of land specially granted to him, free of taxes. A yoke of land measures a hundred Egyptian cubits every way, and the Egyptian cubit happens to be equal to that of Samos. This was a privilege granted to all of them, and they also had certain additional benefits taken in turn, and not by the same men twice. A thousand of the Calasirians and a thousand of the Hermotybians served as bodyguard to the king each year, and besides their yokes of land they received a daily allowance of five pounds of bread per man, two pounds of beef, and four half-pints of wine. This was the allowance given to those serving as the king's bodyguard for the time being.
